ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a straight road, with the road boundaries represented by two parallel solid lines above and below, and a horizontal dashed line in the middle representing the center line. Robert's route is a series of connected semicircular arcs, with the semicircles alternately located above and below the center line; the endpoints of each semicircle are on the dashed center line, and the highest or lowest point of the arc exactly touches the road boundary. Then reason: The road is 40 feet wide, so the distance from the center line to either boundary is 20 feet. Each semicircle goes from the center line to the boundary, so the radius is 20 feet and the diameter is 40 feet. The length along the 1-mile road is 5280 feet, so the number of semicircles needed is 5280 ÷ 40 = 132. The arc length of each semicircle is half a circumference, namely πr = 20π feet. The total distance is 132 × 20π = 2640π feet. Converting to miles: 2640π ÷ 5280 = π/2 miles. Robert's speed is 5 miles/hour, so the time required is (π/2) ÷ 5 = π/10 hours.

raw_record.question_text:
A straight one-mile stretch of highway, 40 feet wide, is closed. Robert rides his bike on a path composed of semicircles as shown. If he rides at 5 miles per hour, how many hours will it take to cover the one-mile stretch?

Note: 1 mile = 5280 feet.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the road is shown as two parallel horizontal boundary lines with a dashed centerline, and Robert's path is made of consecutive semicircles alternating above and below the centerline. Each semicircle has its diameter along the centerline and reaches one road edge, so its radius is half the 40-foot road width, namely 20 feet, and its diameter along the highway is 40 feet. From the text, the highway stretch is 1 mile = 5280 feet and the speed is 5 mph. Count the number of semicircles needed along the one-mile stretch: 5280/40 = 132. Each semicircle has arc length half the circumference of a circle of radius 20, so its length is 20π feet. Total distance is 132 · 20π = 2640π feet = π/2 miles. Time = distance/speed = (π/2)/5 = π/10 hours.
